business_scope.primary_industry_name: Maritime Seafarer Staffing and Vessel Crew Management Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Convention between Canada and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (Canada–China DTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46 (money laundering, bribery, and forfeiture provisions); Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended, and associated corporate registry transparency directives respecting beneficial ownership records; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.) for record-keeping and reporting obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or government-issued photo identification for each beneficial owner, director, and incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary public in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada and signatory states) or Consular Legalization (non-Apostille states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incumbency or corporate registry extract (for corporate shareholders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies of the originating jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / existence for existing corporate beneficial owners
Bank reference letter or source-of-funds declaration signed by each beneficial owner and accompanied by notarized identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Special Economic Measures Act), United Nations Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN List, and World-Check/PEP databases; enhanced due diligence required if any person is a Politically Exposed Person (domestic or foreign), including source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (accessible via the official Government of Alberta corporate registry portal and through authorized NUANS service providers)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or French using Latin script; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into a Latin-script equivalent. The name must be distinctive from all existing names and include a mandatory legal element (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.'). Names that are too general or misleading are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the NUANS name search is rejected, the Alberta Corporate Registry provides written reasons. The applicant may within 30 days file a formal Request for Name Reconsideration with the Registry, submitting legal argument, alternative names, and supporting precedent. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by filing an originating application within the applicable statutory limitation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the registered office as long as it is a physical street address in Alberta where documents can be served, provided it is not a post office box. No industry-specific physical-presence rule applies to a ship crew recruitment agency; however, tax and commercial-substance reviews may require that the registered office is not used merely as a letterbox, and actual management and records should be maintained in Alberta.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~5% annual probability of unannounced inspection by the Alberta Corporate Registry); moderate (~15%) if Transport Canada or Alberta Employment Standards conducts a compliance audit related to crew recruitment operations, which may include on-site record inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Alberta provincial incorporation registration fee (Business Corporations Act)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per government fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and reservation bundle
Registered office and corporate records address (first year)
Notarization and Hague Apostille / Consular legalization bundle for UBO and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Commissioner for Oaths, or consular authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance onboarding kit (UBO declarations, PEP and sanctions screening)
Legal retainer for articles of incorporation and bylaws drafting
GST/HST registration and ABCA post-incorporation regulatory filing preparation (first-year prep)
Alberta employment agency licence (marine crew recruitment) – application and first-year surety bond
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Government of Alberta / Alberta Labour Relations Board

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (ABCA), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 12 (incorporation), 13-18 (articles, name and amendments), 27 (share rights), 97-104 (directors), 108-129 (officers), 119-120 (registered office and records). Supplementary: Corporate Registry Regulation, Alta Reg 227/2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Government of Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under s. 12 ABCA, together with Initial Notices filed under s. 102 and the Business Names Regulation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under ABCA; consideration for shares may be cash, property or past service (s. 23). Directors fix the issue price; no escrow or bank blocking account is required by ABCA for general corporations. For a crew employment agency, a prescribed employment-agency licence bond is required by Alberta's Employment Agency Business Licensing Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscriptions to shares recorded in the subscription register are accepted in full; the directors may issue and allot common shares to subscribing shareholders upon payment of the designated consideration. 2. The registered office is established at [Registered Office Address], Calgary, Alberta, and the registered agent named in the Notice of Registered Office is appointed to accept process. 3. The following officers are appointed for the corporate year: [Name], President; [Name], Secretary; [Name], Treasurer, with duties per the by-laws and ABCA. 4. Opening corporate bank accounts, obtaining the CRA Business Number, and authorizing banking signatories are approved. 5. All prior acts of the incorporator are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through licensed Registry Agents / Law Society of Alberta-authorized providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) pre-screen to obtain a name search report. Submit a name reservation request to the Alberta Corporate Registry (online via a registry agent or at a Service Alberta registry office), requesting that the proposed corporate name be reserved for 90 days. Select an exact-lock form with jurisdiction indicative 'Alberta Ltd.' or 'Corp.' as required by s. 15 ABCA.
required_dossiers: Written consents of any individuals or corporations whose names appear in the proposed name
Government of Alberta service fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may request a reconsideration from the Director of Corporate Registries under s. 12(3) ABCA, or amend the Articles with an alternate approved name; a reserved name may also be renewed for an additional period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (online Corporate Registration service / Registry Agents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation, setting out the corporate name, registered office address, share structure (authorized share classes, rights, restrictions; or no share par value), restrictions on share transfers, the number of first directors, and any supplementary provisions. Upload the signed Articles and required attachments to the Alberta Corporate Registry portal, or present them at a registry agent office, and pay the incorporation fee. Upon approval the registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Valid NUANS name search report (within 90 days)
Consent of each proposed director to act under s. 103(2) ABCA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected, the applicant cures defects by filing amended Articles under s. 17 ABCA or by correcting clerical errors under s. 112, and may pay an expedited review fee to obtain statutory Certificate within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Registered Office and First Directors (Notice of Registered Office / Notice of Directors)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Registered Office (Form 19) and the Notice of Directors (Form 4) within 30 days after incorporation (or include them in the incorporation filing), identifying the street address of the registered office in Alberta and the full names, residential addresses, and director indemnification consents of the first directors. Ensure each director has signed consent to act; the records constitute statutory governance filings.
required_dossiers: Consent from the registered office landlord, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A late filing exposes the corporation to late fees assessed by the Corporate Registry; the remedy is administrative: file the overdue notice with the required late-payment surcharge and, where applicable, seek reinstatement under s. 213 ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Federal Business Number and Program Accounts with CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated entity with the CRA to obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN), and open the applicable program accounts: corporate income tax, GST/HST (≥CAD $30,000 annual revenue threshold), payroll (RZ), and maritime seafarer payroll remittance accounts. Complete the online registration through CRA's Business Registration Online portal, providing the Certificate of Incorporation details, principal business activity (NAICS 488390), and director information.
required_dossiers: Void cheque for payroll direct debit enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA account is blocked or queried, the applicant may correct information via My Business Account within 30 days; voluntary disclosure under CRA Guidance can reduce penalties for late registration and unreported program accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organizational Governance and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent and Corporate Records office of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first organizational meeting of the board of directors (or adopt written resolutions) to adopt by-laws, ratify the first board resolution, approve the issuance of share subscription allotments, elect officers, designate banking signatories, adopt the corporate seal, select the fiscal year end (December 31), and authorize pre-incorporation contracts. Prepare the corporate minute book containing Articles, certificate of incorporation, by-laws, minutes, resolutions, director registers, share transfer register, and registered office record.
required_dossiers: Adopted corporate by-laws (Form 67 or Alberta model by-law)
Share subscription agreements and payment records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective governance acts are curable by a subsequent unanimous shareholder agreement or corrective board resolution under s. 21 ABCA; omitted filings are remedied by late filing and payment of the registry late fee, without loss of corporate existence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Employment Agency Licensing Office, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (provincial), in coordination with Transport Canada Marine Safety Directorate (federal, for marine personnel services under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Employment Agency Licence (Alberta) under the Employment Agency Business Licensing Act, RSA 2000, c E-6; supplementing certification as a ship crew recruitment and placement agency under Marine Personnel Regulations, SOR/2007-115

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (provincial) and Environment and Climate Change Canada (federal, under the Impact Assessment Act)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt/Registration Tier - Category A: a non-industrial administrative office agency; no mandatory EIA screening is triggered absent physical marine staging, crew accommodation, or vessel operation disclosures.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge for standard office operations. If crew scheduling, marine terminal holding, or vessel outfitting is operated: comply with Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA) approval thresholds, CEPA (SOR/2018-71) VOC/VCC emissions, municipal stormwater and wastewater by-laws, and Canadian Shipping Act marine pollution discharge regulations (MARPOL Annexes).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal building occupancy permit and Alberta Fire Code fire-safety inspection for the registered office; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) workplace hazard assessment; compliance certificate from Workers' Compensation Board (WCB-Alberta) confirming payroll coverage; mandatory anti-money-laundering and staff-vetting protocol under FINTRAC customer due diligence standards for payroll and crew logistics.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — sole national tax administrator for federal corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll remittances; also collects Alberta provincial corporate income tax (8%) under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement on behalf of Alberta Treasury Board and Finance / Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration. Primary portal: CRA 'My Business Account' and Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act (federal) or Alberta Business Corporations Act (RSA 2000, c B-9); the corporation is deemed resident in Canada (ITA s. 250(4)(a)). (2) Apply for the CRA Business Number (BN) via BRO, Form RC1, or by phone (1-800-959-5525); the 9-digit BN is the universal tax identifier, with program accounts: RC0001 (corporate income tax), RT0001 (GST/HST), RP0001 (payroll). (3) Foreign/non-resident ownership is fully permitted; provide the Canadian registered office address, director declarations, and, if no Canadian address exists, Form RC460-1 (Canadian Resident Address Information). (4) Register for GST/HST (RT account) once taxable supplies made in Canada exceed CAD 30,000, or voluntarily to recover input tax credits on export-related inputs. (5) No separate Alberta corporate tax account number is required; the CRA administers the Alberta corporate income tax under the same BN. (6) If federally incorporated, file an extra-provincial registration with the Alberta Corporate Registry. (7) Register for a payroll account (RP) before employing personnel in Canada; withhold federal income tax, CPP, and EI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income (ITA ss. 2, 3, 9), with foreign tax credits under s. 126; non-resident corporations are taxed only on Canadian-source business income, employment income, and gains on taxable Canadian property. Standard combined federal + Alberta general corporate rate is 23% for 2025 (15% federal + 8% Alberta); the federal rate is legislated to rise to 16% (2026) and 17% (2027). No Tax_Exempt_Zone exists in Alberta. A Canadian-incorporated entity controlled by non-residents is not a CCPC and therefore cannot claim the Small Business Deduction (combined small-business rate 11%: 9% federal + 2% Alberta on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income). Export service revenue is accrued on the receivable basis.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada; foreign-entity classification follows legal form and CRA administrative guidance (Income Tax Folio S4-F6-C1). Available mechanisms: (a) the Canadian corporation cannot elect pass-through or disregarded status; (b) GST/HST elections: 'Quick Method' (ETA s. 258) and closely-related corporation election (ETA s. 156); (c) non-resident branch tax under ITA s. 219 (25%, treaty-reduced) applies automatically; (d) non-residents with Canadian rental/royalty income may elect net-basis taxation under ITA s. 216(4); (e) ITA s. 113 provides a 90–100% exemption for dividends received from foreign affiliates; (f) proposed/deferred hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.2, 18.21, per the 2021 Fall Economic Statement and subsequent draft legislation, BEPS Action 2) would restrict deductions on hybrid mismatch arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (RSC 1985, c E-15); Alberta is a non-participating province with no provincial sales tax, so only the federal 5% GST component applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — 'small supplier' threshold under ETA s. 239(1): GST/HST registration becomes mandatory once the value of worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada exceeds CAD 30,000 in any calendar quarter or in the four most recent consecutive calendar quarters. Zero-rated export supplies count toward the threshold. Voluntary registration is available to non-residents to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory government API clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control regime is in force in Canada. The CRA operates a voluntary Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing framework based on the international Peppol standard (first certified service providers launched 2023). GST/HST invoices must contain prescribed data (supplier BN, invoice date, recipient identity, description, consideration, tax amount) under ETA ss. 221–223; books and records must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Ship crew recruitment and crewing-management services (ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390) supplied to a non-resident shipowner or operator qualify for GST/HST zero-rating under s. 23(1), Part V, Schedule V, ETA where: (a) the recipient is a non-resident person not registered for GST/HST; (b) the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada; (c) the service is not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed (a pure personnel-procurement service is not customarily 'in respect of' the vessel); and (d) the service is not supplied to an individual present in Canada. No 5% GST is charged on qualifying exports; input tax credits on Canadian overhead are recovered through the net-tax return, producing a refund when credits exceed tax. Risk note: if the contract bundles crew management with services performed on a vessel located in Canadian waters, CRA may recharacterize part of the supply as taxable; contracts should clearly sever pure recruitment services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed crewing service agreement/contract naming the non-resident recipient, vessel(s), and service scope
ETA-compliant GST/HST invoice bearing the supplier Business Number and stating zero-rating under Schedule V, Part V, s. 23(1)
Evidence of recipient non-resident status (foreign certificate of incorporation, foreign tax identifier)
Crew placement manifests and seafarer employment contracts demonstrating services rendered for the non-resident principal
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export consideration
For any ancillary physical goods exports (e.g., marine equipment samples over CAD 2,000): B13A Canadian Export Declaration via CAERS/CITSW, Commercial Invoice, and Bill of Lading
GST/HST net-tax calculations and input tax credit working papers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within the normal 4-year period (ETA s. 298(1)); no limitation period applies for misrepresentation attributable to fraud, neglect, or willful default (ETA s. 298(4)). A false or grossly negligent zero-rating claim triggers a penalty under ETA s. 285.1 equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the net tax; refunds/input tax credits wrongly claimed are clawed back with daily compounded arrears interest (ETA s. 280). Wilful evasion is an offense under ETA s. 327 and Criminal Code s. 380, punishable by fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years (indictable). For income tax, false export-revenue reporting attracts the 50% gross-negligence penalty (ITA s. 163(2)) and prosecution under ITA s. 239. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day export-proceeds repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure is an audit reasonableness benchmark — export receivables remain taxable when 'receivable' under the accrual method, artificial deferral through non-resident receivables may trigger imputed interest under ITA s. 17, and cross-border pricing must satisfy the ITA s. 247 arm's-length standard.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange surveillance overseen by the Department of Finance Canada and bank supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Canada accepts IMF Article VIII obligations, with no restriction on payments for current international transactions, dividends, or profit remittances. The capital account is fully liberalized; share capital injection and shareholder loans into an Alberta corporation are permitted without exchange-control approval. There is no withholding or approval outside the tax regime; outbound profit remittances are subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends (generally 25% under the Income Tax Act, commonly reduced to 5-15% under Canada tax treaties) and applicable CRS/FATCA filing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender rule exists in Canada. There is no statutory timeline or conversion ratio for export receipts. The company may lawfully retain foreign currency proceeds in a Canadian dollar, US dollar, or multi-currency account. The only obligations are trade reporting to Statistics Canada via the Canadian International Merchandise Trade (or the Trade in Services) system and adherence to general FINTRAC record keeping.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium as a supplementary liquidation rail; unacceptable as the sole treasury bank. An offshore digital EMI is not a bank under the Bank Act; to provide payment/FX services to Canadian clients it must be registered with FINTRAC as a money services business (MSB) under the PCMLTFA, meet provincial money lending/transfer registration in Alberta if applicable, and maintain a physical compliance presence or agent relationship. Most non-regulated offshore EMIs fail provincial/AML suitability and are rejected at onboarding. A FINTRAC-registered EMI (e.g., Wise Business, or a chartered-bank-backed payment service provider) can serve crew payroll disbursements in small-value batches but must not hold capital escrow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is effectively mandatory for at least two directors or officers with signing authority, plus the ultimate beneficial owner(s), at most Schedule I Canadian banks. For Canadian resident signatories, remote notarized/validated video verification is sometimes available under a FINTRAC-compliant program, but for this Alberta corporation with permissible non-resident ownership, a physical onboarding meeting at a Calgary or Edmonton commercial banking centre or at the bank's international desk is the practical norm. Remote-only non-resident director onboarding is generally declined or referred to the bank's private/international due diligence branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs and multi-jurisdictional ownership chain with no Canadian ties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) extract; Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing; full ownership org chart and shareholder register; notarized UBO passport plus residential proof; CRS/FATCA self-certifications; bank reference letters from the home-country primary bank covering the last 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between stated ISIC 5222 crew agency activity and forecasted bank traffic (large periodic USD/EUR crew payroll sweeps)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed fee-based manning/crew management agreements with ship owners; sample seafarer employment contracts (STCW-certified); 12-month payroll forward ledger and disbursal schedule; client ship-owner KYC files; corporate registry extracts of vessel owner counterparties; commercial invoice samples and collection/receivables aging report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk destination jurisdictions for outbound payroll (flag states and seafarer home countries classified as high-risk by FATF)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-vetted, closed-loop beneficiary crew list with identity documents; per-beneficiary STCW and seafarer discharge book references; written AML/ATF compliance manual of the agency; third-party sanctions screening results for all beneficiaries and vessel clients; evidence of no cash-pass-through and direct wage-bank transfer wording in every seafarer contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection funded by shareholder loans from offshore low-tax jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed shareholder loan agreement with arm's-length commercial terms (interest, maturity, subordination clause); bank statements showing the source of funds and clearing trail; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; audited or reviewed financial statements of the shareholder; transferred ownership structure memorandum prepared by tax counsel; confirmation that the injection qualifies as paid-up capital or debt for purposes of subsection 15/17 of the Income Tax Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory licensing confirmation for a crew recruitment agency missing or vague
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Employment Agency Business Licensing Regulation licence (if engaging in employment agency activity); Transport Canada's Marine Personnel Regulations (SOR/2007-115) compliance evidence where manning agency services are performed for Canadian-flag vessels; any flag-state manning licence where applicable; corporate business plan; Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN/RT/GST) registration certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation or continuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a Registry notice of strike-off; failure to file two consecutive annual returns permits administrative dissolution under ABCA s 214; reinstatement requires payment of arrears, prescribed reinstatement fee and, where ordered, court approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Federal Annual Return (if the entity is incorporated federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the statement of incorporation; one filing per calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporations Canada may dissolve a corporation for failure to file two consecutive annual returns; revival requires payment of a prescribed revival fee plus arrears and compliance with all outstanding filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate income tax combined filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; no fixed calendar deadline, but a December 31 year-end requires filing by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; compound interest on arrears; repeated non-compliance may result in CRA collection action including garnishment and asset seizure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory revenue or asset threshold applies to private non-distributing Alberta business corporations; a mandatory independent audit applies to distributing or public-issuing corporations, and an auditor must otherwise be appointed unless shareholders unanimously waive the appointment each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Canadian GAAP): IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is available to and commonly selected by private business corporations such as a marine crew recruitment agency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Alberta Business Corporations Act requires private corporations to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC); no separate ISC/UBO declaration is filed annually with the Corporate Registry. Each share transfer or change in significant control must be recorded within 15 days of the corporation learning of the change, and the register must be retained at the registered office and made available for lawful inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100 - USD 400 per year for registered office address services; USD 300 - USD 1,200 per year for registered agent and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 for a small to mid-size private corporation, subject to transaction volume, multi-currency payroll complexity and whether the unanimous shareholder audit waiver is in place

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate rate 15% + Alberta general corporate rate 8% = combined 23%; reduced combined rate for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income: 9% federal + 2% Alberta = 11%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC Small Business Deduction (SBD) lowering combined rate to 11%; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits if eligible R&D is performed; accelerated Capital Cost Allowance (CCA) on eligible depreciable assets; no Alberta-specific tax holiday for crewing agencies; SBD is unavailable if the corporation is controlled by non-residents or is a public corporation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically via CRA-approved software through My Business Account / EFILE for T2; the Alberta corporate income tax return is integrated as T2 Schedule 5 and administered by the CRA under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement; no separate Alberta AT1 is required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual T2 return; quarterly or monthly Part I instalments when tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000; monthly Part XIII non-resident withholding remittances; annual T106 transfer-pricing return; annual T4/NR4 payroll information returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed no later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end = June 30 filing deadline); balance-due date for non-CCPCs is 2 months after year-end and for CCPCs claiming the SBD is 3 months after year-end; instalments are due on the last day of each month or quarter under the 2-month/3-cycle rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) before taxes; accounting net income reconciled to income tax basis via Schedule 1 adjustments to total revenue and expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation incorporated in Canada is a Canadian resident and reports worldwide income; foreign-source crewing management fees are included here and foreign tax credits claimed on Schedule 21 / Form T2209.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting loss carryforwards, capital cost allowance, and treaty-exempt items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document transfer-pricing adjustments on intercompany charges with foreign shipowners and any treaty exemptions for international shipping profits allocated under an applicable DTA Article 8.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part I federal tax payable: 15% general rate, or 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of taxable active business income of a CCPC claiming the SBD.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation controlled by non-resident shareholders is not a CCPC and cannot claim the SBD; verify control structure before completing Schedule 400.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta taxable income and Alberta corporate tax computation: 8% general rate, 2% small business rate on the CCPC threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate taxable income to Alberta using permanent establishment rules; a crewing agency with its principal place of business in Alberta reports 100% of its Canadian business income to Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Small Business Deduction computation (federal 9% rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm CCPC status; any direct or indirect ownership of 50% or more by non-residents disqualifies the SBD claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information return of non-arm's length transactions with non-residents; captures management fees, crew payroll reimbursements, commissions, and loan balances with foreign shipowners or related offshore entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when aggregate controlled transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year; no threshold applies for transactions with residents of a designated non-treaty jurisdiction; attach complete transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable (federal and Alberta) after investment tax credits, foreign tax credits, and instalment payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Part XIII withholding tax remitted on dividends, royalties, and management fees paid to non-residents before the return is authorized by a director or officer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filed T2: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; if the return is filed more than 6 months late, the penalty doubles to 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; minimum penalty CAD 100; gross negligence penalty under s. 163(2) equals 50% of the understated tax; late or deficient Part XIII remittances attract daily compound interest at the CRA prescribed rate plus penalties; failure to file T106 costs CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500 and an additional CAD 1,000 for gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid or credited by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the reduced Canada-US DTA rate (5% where the beneficial owner is a US company holding at least 10% of the voting shares; 15% in other US cases), the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a current Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the relevant foreign tax authority; (2) complete CRA Form NR302 (for corporations) or NR301 (for US individuals) and submit it with the TRC to the Canadian payer before payment; (3) if full 25% WHT was withheld, file CRA Form NR7 with the CRA within two years of the end of the calendar year to claim a refund; the Canadian payer must file NR4 slips and remit Part XIII tax by the 15th day of the month following payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory Part XIII rate 25%; Canada-US treaty 0% or 10% depending on IP type (generally 10% for patents, trademarks, and secret processes; 0% for certain copyright royalties); most other DTAs provide 10-15%. Interest: statutory 25%; under the Canada-US treaty, non-contingent interest is generally exempt from source WHT (0%), while participating or contingent debt interest remains taxable; most DTAs provide 10-15% on related-party interest; Alberta imposes no separate non-resident WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 Information Return must be filed when aggregate non-arm's length transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000 in a fiscal year (no minimum threshold for transactions with residents of designated non-treaty countries); CRA expects contemporaneous Local File documentation for controlled transactions exceeding CAD 5,000,000; a Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated audited revenue of at least CAD 1,000,000,000; the 'reasonable efforts' defence under s. 247(3) requires that the taxpayer prepare and retain contemporaneous documentation before the filing-due date.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply a UAE-style ESR label; instead, the Income Tax Act and the OECD-BEPS framework require real economic substance through: (1) the Place of Effective Management (POEM) test for corporate residency; (2) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, s. 245 ITA); and (3) the 'business carried on in Canada' permanent-establishment doctrine under s. 253 ITA. For an Alberta crew recruitment agency, actual employees, office premises in Alberta, payroll administration functions, and commercially rational decision-making are required; a letterbox or shell structure directing core management functions offshore invites re-characterization, deemed Canadian residency, and reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting foreign crewing revenues from the T2 return, falsifying crew payroll records, creating fictitious invoices to inflate expenses, or participating in a scheme to evade income tax and GST.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 239(1) ITA: on summary conviction, a fine of 50%-200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment of 30 days to 2 years; on indictment, a fine of 100%-200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civilly, the gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under s. 163(2) and compound interest at the prescribed rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are treated as parties to the offense under s. 242 ITA and can be personally fined and imprisoned up to 5 years; CRA may also issue a departure-from-Canada travel ban where the tax debt exceeds CAD 50,000; criminal convictions can trigger additional Criminal Code money-laundering charges (up to 10 years imprisonment).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Alberta corporate registration while placing all board meetings, crew-sourcing decisions, and profit-taking outside Canada to avoid Canadian tax; claiming treaty benefits through a conduit without commercial substance; or using a non-resident nominee to hide the Alberta permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment disregarding the abusive transaction, denial of treaty or SBD benefits, reallocation of income to the Alberta corporation, penalties under s. 163(2) at 50% of the reassessed tax, interest from the original due date, and loss of loss-carryforward utilization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false T2 returns can be charged under s. 239; personal fines and imprisonment up to 5 years; CRA can pierce the corporate veil under s. 160 for non-arm's length transfers of property, making directors jointly and severally liable for the market value transferred.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unremitted Payroll and Non-Resident Withholding Taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using seafarer payroll funds for operations instead of remitting federal and Alberta income tax withholdings, CPP/EI contributions, and Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends or fees paid to foreign shipowners; failure to file T4/T4A/NR4 returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Deemed trust under s. 227(4) over all corporate assets with super-priority over secured creditors; failure to remit penalties of 10% plus 1% per month up to 20 months; interest at the prescribed rate; wilful failure to withhold is an offense punishable by a fine up to CAD 25,000 and/or 12 months imprisonment under s. 227(9); CRA may freeze bank accounts and register a lien against the corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under s. 227.1 for all unremitted source deductions and GST/HST regardless of the corporate veil; the only defense is the exercise of reasonable due diligence, which is assessed strictly; personal liability extends to travel restrictions, seizure of personal assets, and bankruptcy proceedings initiated by the CRA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FINTRAC Non-Compliance on Cross-Border Payroll Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring multi-currency wire transfers to foreign seafarers and shipowners below reporting thresholds to avoid FINTRAC reporting; failing to register as a money service business where currency exchange or remittance services are provided; laundering funds derived from tax evasion through the payroll accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, failure to report a large cash or wire transaction is punishable by administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 500,000 for entities; criminal money laundering under s. 462.31 of the Criminal Code carries imprisonment of up to 10 years and unlimited fines; the CRA and FINTRAC can each pursue concurrent sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly direct, authorize, or acquiesce in structuring transactions are personally chargeable with money laundering offenses; penalties include imprisonment up to 10 years, confiscation of personal and corporate proceeds, and director bans under Canadian corporate law.
